description: How the listening step turns a cell's HH and HV backscatter on the seven dates into sound. Read by app/app.js and by the offline WAV renderer.
mapping: For each date k (0 to 6, in index order) and each voice v (hh, hv): read the byte b. If b == nodata (255) the voice is silent on that beat. Otherwise dB = b / 4 - 40. x = clamp((dB - v.db_min) / (v.db_max - v.db_min), 0, 1). s = min(scale.steps - 1, floor(x * scale.steps)). n = len(scale.intervals). midi = v.base_midi + 12 * floor(s / n) + scale.intervals[s mod n]. freq_hz = 440 * 2 ** ((midi - 69) / 12). peak = v.gain_min + (v.gain_max - v.gain_min) * x. The note starts at t0 = lead_in_s + k * beat_s seconds with an oscillator of shape v.waveform (Web Audio names: sine, triangle) at freq_hz and phase 0. Its amplitude is 0 at t0, rises linearly to peak at t0 + v.attack_s, then decays as peak * exp(-(t - t0 - v.attack_s) / (v.decay_s / 5)) and the note stops at t0 + v.attack_s + v.decay_s. All notes are summed and multiplied by master_gain. Pitch (through s) and loudness (through x) never decrease when dB increases, in both voices, so the mapping is monotonic. With these values the summed peak is at most master_gain * (0.45 + 0.25) = 0.42 of full scale, and one clip lasts lead_in_s + 6 * beat_s + 0.405 s = 3.155 s.
